mainTopic: Two wives and כתובת בנין דכרין: lessons from the משנה, רב אשי's challenges, and the תנאים who argue about one wife dying in the husband's lifetime and one after his death
overview: The גמרא first finishes a point about the משנה's wording: the first clause also uses the word 'precedes.' It then draws three lessons from the משנה's case of a man who married a first wife and then a second. First, the first wife's sons get כתובת בנין דכרין even when one wife died in his lifetime and the other after his death. Second, one wife's כתובה can count as the needed surplus for the other. Third, כתובת בנין דכרין cannot be collected from liened property. רב אשי pushes off the first two lessons by reading the משנה differently. The גמרא then shows that the case of one wife dying in his lifetime and one after his death is argued by the תנאים בן ננס and רבי עקיבא. רבה reports that the רבנן of בי רב saw their argument as being about surplus, and he adds that everyone agrees a creditor's payment counts as surplus. רב יוסף objects from רבי עקיבא's own words and goes back to the first explanation. He then links it to an argument between the תנא קמא and רבי שמעון in a ברייתא; the גמרא begins to push that link off, and the thought continues on the next amud.

steps.title: The first clause uses the same word 'precedes'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא finishes its explanation of the משנה's wording. The earlier clause was also phrased as 'the first precedes the second.'
steps.simpleTranslation: The תנא also taught the first clause the same way: the first wife comes before the second.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is wrapping up a point it began just before this section. The משנה used the word 'precedes' in its first clause too, so the wording there matches the later clause.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'Precedes' only describes the order of payment. It does not mean the second woman must give the money back if she already took it. The תנא kept the same word in both clauses so they would match, without spelling out what happens if she seized the property.

keyTerms.meaning: The teacher of the משנה or ברייתא taught
Comes first, has priority in being paid

phrases.english: He also taught:
phrases.notes: This means the תנא used the same style of wording in the earlier clause of the משנה.

phrases.english: The first woman precedes the second.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues and closes a discussion about the משנה's wording that began before this section.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Explains the wording as parallel phrasing
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Someone might think 'precedes' in the first clause means the second woman must give back what she took.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'Precedes' describes only the order of payment. The same word was used in both clauses so they would match.

steps.title: Three lessons from the משנה; first: no worry about quarreling
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's case of a man who married a first wife. It says three rulings can be learned from it. The first: sons still get כתובת בנין דכרין even when one wife died in the husband's lifetime and the other after his death.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: 'He married the first wife.' Learn three things from it. Learn that if one wife died while he was alive and the other died after his death, they still get כתובת בנין דכרין, and we are not worried that this will lead to quarreling.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new section by quoting the משנה. It announces that three rulings can be drawn from it and states the first one.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally, sons inherit their own mother's כתובה from their father's estate through כתובת בנין דכרין. Here one wife died during the husband's life and the other after his death, so her heirs are claiming in a different way. One might fear this mismatch would cause fights between the brothers. The גמרא says we do not worry about that, and the sons still collect.

keyTerms.meaning: Learn from this, conclude from it
The rule that a wife's sons inherit her כתובה from their father's estate

phrases.english: He married the first woman.
Learn three things from it:
Learn from it that if one died in his lifetime
and one died after his death,
they have a כתובה concerning male children,
and we are not concerned about quarreling.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic by quoting the next case in the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Sons get כתובת בנין דכרין even when one wife died during the husband's life and the other after his death. We do not worry that this will cause quarreling.

steps.title: Proof from the word 'precede'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how we know the first lesson. It proves it from the משנה's wording: the second wife's heirs only 'precede,' so when there is enough money, the first wife's sons also collect.
steps.simpleTranslation: How do we know this? Because the משנה teaches: 'The second wife and her heirs come before the heirs of the first.' They only come first. But if there is enough money for everyone, the first wife's heirs also take their share.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for the source of the first lesson. It answers by reading closely into the משנה's word 'precede.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the first wife's sons had no right at all, the משנה would not say the second wife's heirs 'precede' them. 'Precede' only sets an order of payment. So when there is enough money, the first wife's sons also collect their mother's כתובה, which shows we are not worried about quarreling.

keyTerms.meaning: From where do we know this?

steps.confusionAlert: 'Precede' does not mean the first wife's heirs lose out. It only means they are paid second. When there is enough money, both sides collect.

phrases.english: From where? From the fact that it teaches:
The second wife and her heirs
precede the heirs of the first wife,
they only come first,
but if there is enough, they take.
phrases.notes: 'They' means the first wife's sons, who collect their mother's כתובה when there's enough money.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the first lesson of step 2 from the wording of the משנה.
steps.raayaObject: That sons still get כתובת בנין דכרין when one wife died in the husband's lifetime and the other after his death, with no worry about quarreling.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה's wording 'שְׁנִיָּה וְיוֹרְשֶׁיהָ קוֹדְמִים לְיוֹרְשֵׁי רִאשׁוֹנָה.' The word 'precede' implies the first wife's heirs collect when there is enough money.

steps.title: Second lesson: one כתובה counts as surplus for the other
steps.stepSummary: The second lesson from the משנה: one wife's כתובה can serve as the 'extra' money needed so that the other wife's sons can collect.
steps.simpleTranslation: And learn from it that one כתובה becomes the extra amount for the other.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the second of the three lessons from the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: כתובת בנין דכרין is only paid when there is extra money left, at least a דינר, so that regular תורה inheritance still happens. The משנה lets the first wife's sons collect even when their payment uses everything up. That shows the second wife's כתובה, which is a debt of the whole estate, can count as that extra money.

keyTerms.meaning: Surplus, the extra money left over
Her fellow, the other wife's כתובה

steps.whatToRemember: So far, two of the three lessons: (1) sons get כתובת בנין דכרין even when one wife died during the husband's life and the other after, with no worry about quarreling; (2) one כתובה can count as the needed surplus for the other.

phrases.english: And learn from it:
One כתובה becomes the surplus for the other.
phrases.notes: 'Surplus' is the extra money, at least a דינר, that has to be left for regular inheritance before the sons can collect their mother's כתובה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the second of the three lessons announced in step 2.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: One wife's כתובה can count as the surplus needed for the other wife's sons to collect כתובת בנין דכרין.

steps.title: Proof that one wife's כתובה can count as the extra money
steps.stepSummary: The proof for the second lesson: the משנה never requires an extra דינר here.
steps.simpleTranslation: How do we know this? Because the משנה does not say 'if there is an extra דינר left over.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks how we know the second lesson from Step 4. It points to something the משנה leaves out.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Usually, the sons can only collect their mothers' כתובות if there is at least a דינר left over beyond them. Here the משנה lets the first wife's sons collect without mentioning that condition. So the second wife's כתובה itself must be acting as the needed 'extra.'

keyTerms.meaning: From where do we know this?
An extra דינר left over beyond the כתובות
It teaches / it says (in the משנה)

phrases.english: From where do we know this?
From the fact that it does not teach
"If there is an extra דינר there."
phrases.notes: This condition appears in the משנה's other case, where both wives died first. Here the משנה leaves it out.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supplies the proof for the second lesson stated in Step 4.
steps.raayaObject: That one wife's כתובה can serve as the 'extra money' for the other wife's sons.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה's silence about the requirement of an extra דינר in this case.

steps.title: Third lesson: male sons' כתובה is not taken from sold property
steps.stepSummary: The third lesson from the משנה: כתובת בנין דכרין cannot be collected from liened property.
steps.simpleTranslation: And learn from it: the כתובה of male sons cannot be collected from property that is liened (already sold or committed to others).
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא states the third lesson it learns from this משנה. The proof comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A normal creditor can take back land the debtor sold after the loan. The sons collecting כתובת בנין דכרין do not get this power. They can only collect from what is still freely in the estate.

keyTerms.meaning: Liened property: property already committed or sold to others

phrases.english: And learn from it:
the כתובה of male sons
does not seize from liened property,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds the third of the three lessons announced in Step 2.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: כתובת בנין דכרין cannot be collected from liened (sold) property.

steps.title: Proof: otherwise the first wife's sons would beat the second wife's heirs
steps.stepSummary: If male sons could take from liened property, the first wife's sons would take from the second wife's heirs, but the משנה says the second wife's heirs come first.
steps.simpleTranslation: For if you thought it could be collected from liened property, then the first wife's sons should come and take it away from the second wife's sons.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא proves the third lesson by showing what would go wrong if it were not true.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first wife's כתובה was written earlier, so her claim on the father's land is older. If her sons could seize property like a creditor, their older claim would let them take back what the second wife's heirs collected. Since the משנה says the second wife's heirs 'precede,' the sons must not have that creditor's power.

keyTerms.meaning: If it would enter our mind (if you thought that)
The sons of the first wife

phrases.english: For if it would enter our mind
that it seizes from liened property,
then let the sons of the first wife come
and seize it from the sons of the second wife.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Proves the third lesson stated in Step 6.
steps.raayaObject: That כתובת בנין דכרין cannot be collected from liened property.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה's ruling that the second wife's heirs 'precede' the first wife's heirs.
steps.whatToRemember: Three lessons from the משנה: (1) sons get כתובת בנין דכרין even when one wife died before the husband and one after him; (2) one wife's כתובה can serve as the 'extra'; (3) כתובת בנין דכרין is not collected from liened property.

steps.title: רב אשי: maybe 'precede' only refers to regular inheritance
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי suggests that in this case there may be no כתובת בנין דכרין at all. 'Precede' would then only mean the remaining estate is split as a normal inheritance.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי objects: How do you know? Maybe I can really tell you that when one wife died in his lifetime and one after his death, there is no כתובת בנין דכרין at all. And what does 'precede' mean? It is talking about the regular inheritance.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי challenges the lessons just learned. He offers a different reading of the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first lesson depended on reading 'precede' as 'the first wife's sons also collect their mother's כתובה afterward.' רב אשי reads it differently. The second wife's heirs collect her כתובה first, and then all the sons split what is left as normal heirs of their father. If he is right, the משנה does not prove that lesson. Step 11 then pushes off the second lesson as well.

phrases.english: רב אשי objects to it:
From where do you know?
Perhaps I can really say to you
that when one died in his lifetime and one after his death,
they have no כתובה of male sons,
and what does "precede" mean?
It is teaching about regular inheritance.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the reading of 'precede' that the lessons in Steps 2–7 were built on.
steps.kashyaTarget: The first lesson, which was drawn from the משנה's word 'precede.'
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: 'Precede' can also be read as referring only to normal inheritance. In that case the first wife's sons never collect כתובת בנין דכרין here, and the proof of the first lesson falls away.
steps.confusionAlert: רב אשי is not saying the second wife's heirs lose anything. They still collect her כתובה first. He only questions whether the first wife's sons get their mother's כתובה afterward.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The first lesson (steps 2–3): that the first wife's sons get כתובת בנין דכרין when one wife died in his lifetime and one after his death.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: 'קודמין' can refer to regular inheritance (לנחלה). In that reading, the first wife's sons may have no כתובת בנין דכרין here at all, so the word 'precede' proves nothing.

steps.title: Why mention 'the heirs of the first wife'?
steps.stepSummary: An expected challenge to רב אשי: if this is ordinary inheritance from the father, why does the משנה call them heirs of the first wife?
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you will say: why do I need the words 'the heirs of the first wife'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא raises a possible challenge to רב אשי's reading. The answer comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Under רב אשי's reading, the first wife's sons inherit as their father's sons, not through their mother. So calling them 'heirs of the first wife' seems to point to a claim through their mother, which is the כתובה.

keyTerms.meaning: The heirs of the first wife

phrases.english: And if you will say:
why do I need "the heirs of the first wife"?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Raises a possible challenge to רב אשי's reading in Step 8.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב אשי's claim that the משנה is only talking about inheritance from the father.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה's wording 'heirs of the first wife' suggests a claim that comes through the mother, not just through the father.

steps.title: Matching wording: the משנה just mirrors 'the second and her heirs'
steps.stepSummary: The משנה said 'heirs of the first' only to match its phrase 'the second wife and her heirs.'
steps.simpleTranslation: Since it taught 'the second wife and her heirs,' it also taught 'the heirs of the first wife.'
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי's side answers the challenge. The wording is just a stylistic match and proves nothing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The second wife's heirs really do collect through their mother, because her כתובה is a debt. The משנה used parallel wording for the first wife's sons to keep the sentence balanced. That does not mean they collect their mother's כתובה.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is a common move in the גמרא: a word can be explained as matching nearby wording, so it does not teach a separate law.

phrases.english: Since it taught "the second wife and her heirs,"
it also taught "to the heirs of the first wife."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 9 and defends רב אשי's reading.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Stylistic parallelism: the wording is explained as matching nearby wording, so it teaches no separate law.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'Heirs of the first wife' shows that the first wife's sons collect through their mother's כתובה.
steps.terutzMaskana: The phrase only mirrors 'the second wife and her heirs.' The first wife's sons may simply be inheriting from their father.
steps.whatToRemember: According to רב אשי, this משנה may teach only that the second wife's כתובה is paid first, with the rest split as normal inheritance. So the first lesson cannot be proven from it. The next step pushes off the second lesson as well.

steps.title: Pushing off the proof that one כתובה can serve as the surplus for the other
steps.stepSummary: The lesson 'one כתובה becomes surplus for the other' is rejected. Our case may simply have one extra דינר left over.
steps.simpleTranslation: And what you said, that one כתובה becomes the surplus for the other one: maybe I can really tell you that one כתובה does NOT become the surplus for the other. Here we are dealing with a case where there is an extra דינר left over.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי continues his objection. He goes back to the second lesson drawn from the משנה and shows it is not proven, since the משנה could be talking about an estate that has a leftover דינר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The earlier claim was that one wife's כתובה can count as the required 'extra' amount that allows the other wife's sons to collect כתובת בנין דכרין. The rejection says the משנה may simply be speaking of an estate with an extra דינר, so nothing can be learned from it. The משנה did not mention the דינר because that detail was not its topic.

keyTerms.meaning: For her fellow, meaning the other wife's כתובה
A coin. Here it is the small extra amount left over in the estate

steps.whatToRemember: רב אשי has now pushed off two of the three lessons drawn from the משנה: the one about one wife dying in his lifetime and one after his death, and the one about one כתובה serving as surplus for the other. The גמרא does not challenge the third lesson, about liened property.

phrases.english: And what you said: one marriage contract becomes surplus for the other
perhaps I could actually say to you:
one marriage contract does not become surplus for the other,
and here it is a case where there is a surplus of a dinar.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּדְקָאָמְרַתְּ: כְּתוּבָּה נַעֲשֵׂית מוֹתָר לַחֲבֶרְתָּהּ — דִּלְמָא לְעוֹלָם אֵימָא לָךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the series of rejections, now aimed at a different lesson drawn from the משנה
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The inference that one כתובה serves as the required surplus for the other
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The משנה may be dealing with an estate that has an extra דינר, so it proves nothing about this rule

steps.title: The case of one wife dying before and one after the husband is a תנאים dispute: בן ננס's view
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא says the case of one wife dying in his lifetime and one after his death is argued by תנאים. בן ננס lets the first wife's sons tell the second wife's sons to take their mother's כתובה and leave.
steps.simpleTranslation: The case of 'one in his lifetime and one after his death' is a dispute between תנאים. A ברייתא teaches: if they died, one in his lifetime and one after his death, בן ננס says the first wife's sons can say to the second wife's sons: 'You are sons of a creditor. Take your mother's כתובה and leave.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the case רב אשי questioned (one wife died in his lifetime and one after his death) and says תנאים argue about it. It quotes a ברייתא, starting with בן ננס's opinion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The second wife outlived the husband, so her כתובה is a debt the estate owes, and her sons collect it like creditors. According to בן ננס, after that debt is paid, the first wife's sons take what is left through their mother's כתובת בנין דכרין.

keyTerms.meaning: It is a dispute between תנאים
A creditor, someone who is owed money

phrases.english: 'And one in his lifetime and one after his death' —
is a dispute of Tannaim,

phrases.aramaic: דְּתַנְיָא: מֵתוּ אַחַת בְּחַיָּיו וְאַחַת בְּמוֹתוֹ,
phrases.english: as it is taught: If they died, one in his lifetime and one after his death,
ben Nanas says:

phrases.aramaic: יְכוֹלִין בְּנֵי הָרִאשׁוֹנָה לוֹמַר לִבְנֵי הַשְּׁנִיָּה:
phrases.english: The sons of the first can say to the sons of the second:
You are sons of a creditor,
take your mother's marriage contract and leave.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Takes the very case רב אשי just questioned (one wife died in his lifetime and one after his death) and shows that תנאים already argue about it.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to בן ננס, the first wife's sons collect כתובת בנין דכרין even though the second wife outlived the husband

steps.title: רבי עקיבא: the inheritance already passed away from the first wife's sons
steps.stepSummary: רבי עקיבא disagrees. The inheritance has already jumped away from the first wife's sons and landed with the second wife's sons.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי עקיבא says: the inheritance has already jumped away from the sons of the first wife and fallen to the sons of the second wife.
steps.whatsHappening: This is the other side of the ברייתא. רבי עקיבא rejects בן ננס's claim for the first wife's sons.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי עקיבא holds that in this case the first wife's sons do not get their special claim. After the second wife's כתובה is paid, the rest of the estate is split as a regular inheritance among all the sons.

keyTerms.meaning: Fell before, meaning it came into their hands

phrases.english: Rabbi Akiva says:
The inheritance has already jumped
away from the sons of the first
and fallen before the sons of the second.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא אוֹמֵר: כְּבָר קָפְצָה נַחֲלָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the opposing view in the same ברייתא
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי עקיבא, the first wife's sons do not have a special claim in this case

steps.title: Suggesting the dispute is about whether כתובת בנין דכרין applies here
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests what the argument is about. בן ננס holds that כתובת בנין דכרין applies when one wife died before the husband and one after him, and רבי עקיבא holds it does not.
steps.simpleTranslation: Isn't it that they argue about this? One master holds that when one wife died in his lifetime and one after his death, there is כתובת בנין דכרין. The other master holds that in that case there is no כתובת בנין דכרין.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא proposes the reason behind the argument between בן ננס and רבי עקיבא. This sets up the next move, where the גמרא will check whether this reading is really necessary.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words 'מאי לאו' offer a suggested reading, not a final ruling. If the suggestion holds, then whether כתובת בנין דכרין applies in this case is a real dispute between תנאים. That would back up the claim made at the start of step 12.

keyTerms.meaning: Isn't it that? The opening of a suggested reading
The כתובה of male sons: a mother's כתובה that passes to her own sons

steps.confusionAlert: 'מאי לאו' usually opens a suggestion that the גמרא may soon push off. Do not treat this step as the final conclusion yet.

phrases.english: What, is it not that they argue about this:

phrases.aramaic: דְּמָר סָבַר: אַחַת בְּחַיָּיו וְאַחַת בְּמוֹתוֹ —
phrases.english: that one master holds: one in his lifetime and one after his death —
phrases.notes: The first 'master' is בן ננס, and the second one is רבי עקיבא.

phrases.english: they have the marriage contract of male sons,

phrases.aramaic: וּמָר סָבַר: אַחַת בְּחַיָּיו וְאַחַת בְּמוֹתוֹ —
phrases.english: and the other master holds: one in his lifetime and one after his death —
they do not have the marriage contract of male sons.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the ברייתא from steps 12 and 13 to show what the תנאים argue about
steps.raayaObject: The claim that the case of one wife dying in his lifetime and one after his death is a תנאים dispute
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא of בן ננס and רבי עקיבא, read as arguing over whether כתובת בנין דכרין applies

steps.title: The Sages of the school of רב explain the argument differently
steps.stepSummary: רבה reports that the רבנן of בי רב said everyone agrees about one wife in his lifetime and one after his death. The argument is really about whether one כתובה can count as the surplus for the other, and the same goes for a creditor.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה said: I found the Sages of the school of רב sitting and saying: Everyone agrees that when one wife died in his lifetime and one after his death, the sons collect כתובת בנין דכרין. Here, they argue about whether one כתובה becomes the surplus for the other, and the same goes for a creditor.
steps.whatsHappening: רבה brings a different explanation of the argument between בן ננס and רבי עקיבא. It replaces the suggestion from Step 14.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 14 said the argument was about whether כתובת בנין דכרין applies at all in the case of one wife in his life and one after his death. The רבנן of בי רב say everyone agrees that it does apply. The real question is whether the second wife's כתובה can count as the needed 'extra' money, and the same question applies to money paid to a creditor.

keyTerms.meaning: The Sages of the school of רב
The rule that a wife's sons inherit her כתובה from their father's estate
Surplus, the extra money left over
A creditor, someone the father owed money to

steps.confusionAlert: This is the same case as before. Only the explanation of what the תנאים are arguing about has changed.

phrases.english: Rabba said:
I found the Sages of the school of Rav
sitting and saying:

phrases.aramaic: דְּכוּלֵּי עָלְמָא אַחַת בְּחַיָּיו וְאַחַת בְּמוֹתוֹ
phrases.english: Everyone agrees that when one wife died in his lifetime and one after his death,
the sons are entitled to the marriage contract concerning male children.
Here, they disagree about whether one marriage contract becomes surplus for the other,
and the same is true for payment to a creditor.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבָּה, אַשְׁכַּחְתִּינְהוּ לְרַבָּנַן דְּבֵי רַב דְּיָתְבִי וְקָאָמְרִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects Step 14's explanation of the argument and offers a new one.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The idea that בן ננס and רבי עקיבא argue about whether כתובת בנין דכרין applies when one wife died in his life and one after his death.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: Everyone agrees it applies. The argument is about what counts as surplus.

steps.title: Spelling out each side's view
steps.stepSummary: One Sage holds that a כתובה, and also a creditor's payment, counts as surplus. The other Sage holds that neither does.
steps.simpleTranslation: One Sage holds that a כתובה becomes surplus for the other, and the same goes for a creditor. The other Sage holds that a כתובה does not become surplus for the other, and the same goes for a creditor.
steps.whatsHappening: The רבנן of בי רב lay out the two sides of the argument they just described.
steps.deeperAnalysis: בן ננס says the money paid out for one כתובה, or to a creditor, can count as the needed extra, so the sons may collect. רבי עקיבא says it cannot, so the inheritance 'jumped' to the second wife's sons. In this view, the creditor and the כתובה follow the same rule.

phrases.english: One Sage holds:
one marriage contract becomes surplus for the other,
and the same is true for a creditor;
and one Sage holds:
one marriage contract does not become surplus for the other,
and the same is true for a creditor.

steps.triggerLanguage: מָר סָבַר: כְּתוּבָּה נַעֲשֵׂית מוֹתָר לַחֲבֶרְתָּהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the two positions in the argument described in Step 15.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: בן ננס: a כתובה or a creditor's payment counts as surplus. רבי עקיבא: neither counts.

steps.title: רבה: everyone agrees about a creditor
steps.stepSummary: רבה told them that a creditor's payment counts as surplus according to everyone. The argument is only about a כתובה.
steps.simpleTranslation: And I said to them: about a creditor, everyone agrees that it counts as surplus. Where they argue is about a כתובה.
steps.whatsHappening: רבה gives his own view and narrows the argument of the רבנן of בי רב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The רבנן said the creditor and the כתובה follow the same rule. רבה separates them: everyone agrees that paying a creditor counts as surplus, and בן ננס and רבי עקיבא argue only about whether a כתובה counts.

phrases.english: And I said to them:

phrases.aramaic: בְּבַעַל חוֹב כּוּלֵּי עָלְמָא לָא פְּלִיגִי
phrases.english: with regard to a creditor, everyone agrees
that it is considered surplus.
Where they disagree is about a marriage contract.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Narrows the explanation from Steps 15 and 16 by taking the creditor out of the argument.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Paying a creditor counts as surplus according to everyone. The argument is only about a כתובה.

steps.title: רב יוסף: רבי עקיבא's wording does not fit
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף challenges this. If the argument is about what counts as surplus, רבי עקיבא should have said 'if there is an extra דינר,' not 'the inheritance already jumped.'
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף challenged this: If so, why does רבי עקיבא say 'the inheritance already jumped'? He should have said 'if there is a surplus of a דינר'!
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף attacks the explanation of רבה and the רבנן by pointing to רבי עקיבא's exact words.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the real question were about counting the money as surplus, רבי עקיבא would have said, 'The sons collect only if there is an extra דינר.' Instead he said 'the inheritance already jumped,' which sounds like an argument about the case itself. That fits Step 14's explanation better.

phrases.english: Rav Yosef objects to this:
If that is so,
why does it say: 'Rabbi Akiva says: The inheritance already jumped away'?
He should have said: 'If there is a surplus of a dinar'!

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְקֵיף לַהּ רַב יוֹסֵף: אִי הָכִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the explanation given in Steps 15 to 17.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim of רבה and the רבנן of בי רב that the argument is about whether a כתובה counts as surplus.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי עקיבא's wording, 'the inheritance already jumped,' does not match an argument about surplus. That kind of argument would be worded as 'if there is an extra דינר.'

steps.title: רב יוסף returns to the first explanation
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף says the argument between בן ננס and רבי עקיבא really is about one wife dying in the husband's lifetime and one after his death.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רב יוסף said: They argue about a case where one wife died while he was alive and one after he died.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף's question showed that the 'surplus' explanation does not fit רבי עקיבא's words. So he goes back to the first explanation of the argument.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 15 the רבנן of בי רב said everyone agrees about this case. רב יוסף now rejects that idea. He says the real argument is whether כתובת בנין דכרין applies at all when one wife died before the husband and one after. This fits רבי עקיבא's words 'the inheritance already jumped.'

keyTerms.meaning: Rather. It drops the earlier idea and gives a new one
One wife died in his lifetime and one after his death

phrases.english: Rather, Rav Yosef said:
About one wife who died in his lifetime and one who died after his death
they disagree.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Follows from רב יוסף's question in step 18. It throws out the 'surplus' explanation and brings back the explanation from step 14.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefining what the argument is about
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The argument was about whether one כתובה can count as the 'surplus' for the other.
steps.terutzMaskana: The argument is about whether כתובת בנין דכרין applies at all when one wife died before the husband and one after.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: בן ננס and רבי עקיבא argue about whether כתובת בנין דכרין applies at all when one wife died in the husband's lifetime and one after his death.

steps.title: A matching argument in a ברייתא
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא says the argument of בן ננס and רבי עקיבא matches an argument in a ברייתא between a תנא קמא and רבי שמעון about a man who had two wives.
steps.simpleTranslation: These תנאים are like those תנאים. A ברייתא teaches: A man married a first wife and she died. Then he married a second wife and he died. The sons of this wife come after death and collect their mother's כתובה. רבי שמעון says: If there is one extra דינר, these sons collect their mother's כתובה and those sons collect their mother's כתובה. If not, they split everything equally.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא with an argument it says is just like the one between בן ננס and רבי עקיבא. This sets up the next step, which explains exactly how the two arguments match.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The case is the same: the first wife died during the husband's life and the second after his death. The תנא קמא only mentions one set of sons collecting their mother's כתובה. רבי שמעון says both sets of sons collect if there is an extra דינר, and if not, everyone splits equally.

keyTerms.meaning: תנאים, the Sages of the משנה and ברייתא period

phrases.english: And these tannaim are like those tannaim,
phrases.notes: 'These' means בן ננס and רבי עקיבא. 'Those' means the תנאים in the ברייתא that comes next.

phrases.english: as it is taught in a baraita:
If he married the first woman and she died,
and he married the second woman and he died,

phrases.aramaic: בָּאִין בָּנֶיהָ שֶׁל זוֹ לְאַחַר מִיתָה
phrases.english: the sons of this one come after death
and collect their mother's marriage contract.
Rabbi Shimon says:
If there is a surplus of a dinar,
these collect their mother's marriage contract,
phrases.notes: 'These' are the first wife's sons, and 'these' in the next line are the second wife's sons.

phrases.english: and these collect their mother's marriage contract.
And if not, they divide equally.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָנֵי תַּנָּאֵי כִּי הָנֵי תַּנָּאֵי, דְּתַנְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on רב יוסף's explanation by finding a ברייתא with an argument that seems to match it.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: In the ברייתא, the תנא קמא says the second wife's sons collect their mother's כתובה. רבי שמעון says both sets of sons collect if there is an extra דינר, and if not, they all split equally.

steps.title: Showing how the two arguments match
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests that רבי שמעון holds כתובת בנין דכרין applies when one wife died before the husband and one after, and the תנא קמא holds it does not.
steps.simpleTranslation: Is it not that this is what they argue about? One Sage holds that when one wife died in his lifetime and one after his death, the sons get כתובת בנין דכרין. The other Sage holds that in that case, they do not get כתובת בנין דכרין.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא spells out how the argument in the ברייתא is the same as רב יוסף's explanation of בן ננס and רבי עקיבא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי שמעון lets the first wife's sons collect their mother's כתובה, so he holds כתובת בנין דכרין applies here. The תנא קמא only mentions the second wife's sons collecting, so he holds it does not apply. If this reading is right, it supports רב יוסף's explanation.

keyTerms.meaning: Is it not that...? Used to suggest a reading of a source
The rule that a wife's sons inherit her כתובה money after their father dies

phrases.english: What, is it not that they disagree about this:
that one Sage holds:
phrases.notes: This first Sage is רבי שמעון.

phrases.english: When one wife died in his lifetime and one after his death,
they are entitled to the marriage contract concerning male children,
and the other Sage holds:
When one wife died in his lifetime and one after his death,
they are not entitled to the marriage contract concerning male children.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains exactly how the ברייתא in step 20 matches רב יוסף's explanation in step 19.
steps.raayaObject: רב יוסף's claim that the argument is about whether כתובת בנין דכרין applies when one wife died before the husband and one after.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The argument between the תנא קמא and רבי שמעון in the ברייתא.

steps.title: Maybe everyone agrees the sons collect
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא pushes back: maybe both the תנא קמא and רבי שמעון agree that כתובת בנין דכרין applies when one wife died before the husband and one after.
steps.simpleTranslation: No. Everyone agrees that when one wife died in his lifetime and one after his death, the sons get כתובת בנין דכרין...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the reading from step 21. It starts to say that both תנאים agree on the basic rule. The sentence continues in the next part of the daf.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If everyone agrees the sons collect in this case, the ברייתא does not argue about the same thing as רב יוסף's explanation. So their argument must be about something else, which the גמרא will explain next.

keyTerms.meaning: No. Used to reject a suggested reading

steps.confusionAlert: This is not the end of the thought. The גמרא has only said what both sides agree on, and the actual point of their argument comes right after this.

phrases.english: No,
everyone agrees that
when one wife died in his lifetime and one after his death,
they are entitled to the marriage contract concerning male children,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the suggestion in step 21 that the ברייתא argues about the same issue as רב יוסף's explanation.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects only the proof from the ברייתא. It does not say רב יוסף's explanation of בן ננס and רבי עקיבא is wrong.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: Both תנאים in the ברייתא may agree that כתובת בנין דכרין applies in this case, so their argument must be about something else.
